div.div:
prŏphēto , no
I.perf., 1, ātum, āre, v. a. id., to foretell, predict, prophesy (eccl. Lat.; cf.: praedico, vaticinor): docet, instruit, prophetat, Prud. στεφ. 13, 101: “servi prophetaturi,” Tert. Anim. 47 : “mors Christi prophetata,” id. adv. Marc. 3, 19 fin. ; id. Res. Carn. 28; Vulg. Matt. 15, 7 et saep.—Perf.: “PROPHETAVIT,” Inscr. Orell. 4872 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
